title: Domain Registrations Maximum-Term Extension: Years and Amount
content:
**Pricing desk computation schedule — maximum-term extensions of Domain Registrations domains**

A maximum-term extension is priced only after the domain's status reads active, its maximum-term years being counted from the expiry date the domain then carries.

## A. Maximum-term years

The maximum-term years are worked out from the whole months from the day of the order to the expiry date recorded on the domain, a month counting only once its day of the month is reached: they are the TLD's maximum registration term in years times 12, less those whole months, less one more month where the expiry date does not fall on the same day of the month as the day of the order, divided by 12 and rounded down to a whole number. Where the maximum-term years come to zero, no extension is billed.

## B. Amount

The amount of a maximum-term extension is the maximum-term renewal component, less the maximum-term credits, plus the TLD's ICANN fee for each of the maximum-term years.

- **Maximum-term renewal component:** the TLD's renewal price times the maximum-term years, reduced by the percentage discount that applies to the order, rounded half up to the cent. The ICANN fee is never discounted.
- **Maximum-term credits:** the amounts named as one of the maximum-term credits, added together.
- **ICANN fee:** the TLD's ICANN fee per year times the maximum-term years.

The amount is worked out in this order: first the maximum-term renewal component; then the maximum-term credits are subtracted from it and that result is never taken below zero; and then the ICANN fee is added, every figure being in USD to the cent. Where no percentage discount applies to the order, the component is the renewal price times the years itself; where no maximum-term credit applies, nothing is subtracted.

## C. Worked figures (hypothetical prices: renewal USD 40.00, ICANN fee USD 0.30 per year; maximum registration term 10 years)

1. Order on 12 March 2028, expiry date 20 October 2030. Whole months from 12 March 2028 to 20 October 2030: 31. The days of the month differ, so one more month is taken off: 120 months less 31 less 1 leaves 88 months; divided by 12 that is 7.33, rounded down to **7 years**. The new expiry date would be 20 October 2037, within 10 years of the order day.
2. Order on 5 June 2028, expiry date 5 June 2029. Whole months: 12, same day of the month, so 120 less 12 leaves 108 months, exactly **9 years**; the new expiry date of 5 June 2038 is exactly 10 years after the order day.
3. Amount for case 1 with no discount and no credit: component 7 times USD 40.00, that is USD 280.00; ICANN fee 7 times USD 0.30, that is USD 2.10; amount USD 282.10.
4. Amount for case 1 where credits of USD 300.00 were named: USD 280.00 less USD 300.00 is taken as zero, and the ICANN fee of USD 2.10 is added; amount USD 2.10.
